卡瑞尔的日记

entries.en: I came to visit my Grandparent's tomb inside the Catacombs, and pay my respects. When I finally arrived I discovered the tombs had been destroyed, someone had dug up the bodies! Who would do such an evil thing?
entries.zh: 我来到地下墓穴，想去祖父母的墓前祭拜。可等我终于赶到时，却发现墓已经被毁了，有人把遗体挖走了！谁会做出这么恶毒的事？

entries.en: I noticed two parallel streaks connecting the uncovered grave site to a tunnel I had never seen before inside the Catacombs. Whoever decided to desecrate a sacred burial ground and drag the bodies away, they will surely pay!
entries.zh: 我注意到有两道平行的拖痕，从被掘开的墓穴一直延伸到一条我在地下墓穴里从没见过的隧道。不管是谁亵渎了这片神圣的墓地、把遗体拖走，都一定会付出代价！

entries.en: After I exited the tunnel, I came upon a large room. It was inlaid with many skulls, a plethora of its stonework was deeply cracked, the wooden tiles completely rotten, and cobwebs littered the ceiling, as if no one stepped foot in here for years.
entries.zh: 穿出隧道后，我来到一个大房间。墙上嵌满了头骨，石砌的墙面大多裂开了深深的缝，木地板全都烂透了，天花板上挂满蛛网，好像很多年都没人踏足过这里。

entries.en: I heard something, a deep growl, and it was coming from deeper inside of the tunnel. I need to go further and keep following this trail, but I can't help being afraid at what possibly lurks inside.
entries.zh: 我听到了什么声音，一声低沉的咆哮，是从隧道更深处传来的。我得继续往里走，顺着这条痕迹追下去，可我忍不住害怕，不知道里面到底藏着什么。

entries.en: As I relentlessly pursued the body snatcher, I heard the groans get louder and louder. Although I was scared, I gathered up my courage and kept going. As I turned the corner I saw it.
entries.zh: 我紧追着那个盗尸者不放，呻吟声越来越响。虽然害怕，我还是鼓起勇气继续前进。拐过墙角时，我看见了它。

entries.en: Carefully picking up the remnants of a broken sword beside me, I slowly began to approach it. As I was nearing combat distance, I stepped on a bone, alerting the creature. As it turned around, I dropped my weapon, and my face turned pale.
entries.zh: 我小心地捡起身旁一把断剑的残片，慢慢朝它靠近。就快到能动手的距离时，我踩到了一根骨头，惊动了那个怪物。它转过身来的那一刻，我手里的武器掉在了地上，脸色变得惨白。

entries.en: It was a distorted face of sorrow and anguish. Pieces of flesh were slowly falling off her, as if she was a rotten fruit. It was the face of my Grandma. "G-grandma, is that you?" I asked with expectation, but my own naivety betrayed me.
entries.zh: 那是一张因悲伤和痛苦而扭曲的脸。一块块腐肉正从她身上慢慢剥落，就像一只烂掉的水果。那是我祖母的脸。“奶……奶奶，是你吗？”我满怀期待地问，可我的天真出卖了我。

entries.en: It stepped towards me, a cruel grin stretching her face to unbelievable proportions. That face terrified me, I even threw up. Then she - no - it lunged at me.
entries.zh: 它朝我走来，残忍的笑容把她的脸撑大到不可思议的地步。那张脸吓坏了我，我甚至吐了出来。然后她——不——是它，朝我扑了过来。

entries.en: With tears flowing down my face, I turned around and began running.
entries.zh: 我泪流满面，转身就跑。

entries.en: I don't know how long I ran for, but the feeling in my legs gave out long ago. "That wasn't her, there's no way!" I wanted to plead for help, I wanted someone to comfort me. But deep down I knew the truth, and that help would never come.
entries.zh: 我不知道自己跑了多久，双腿早就没了知觉。“那不是她，绝对不可能！”我想求救，想有人来安慰我。可我心底很清楚真相，也知道永远不会有人来救我。

entries.en: Worn out, I finally backtracked to the tunnel's entrance. "I need to report this to the Mage Association, they can solve this predicament!" But what happened was most definitely evil magic.
entries.zh: 精疲力竭的我终于原路退回到隧道入口。“我得把这件事报告给法师协会，他们能解决这场危机！”但发生的这一切，毫无疑问是邪恶的魔法。
研究记录

entries.en: This is the lab report of Dr. Myles, Scientist of the Mage Association, in conjunction with Officer Roy of the Adventurer's Guild, and Documentation of the Catacombs. Roy will be my assistant with this, and also in future Lab Reports.
entries.zh: 这是法师协会科学家迈尔斯博士的实验报告，与冒险者公会的罗伊警官合作完成，并附地下墓穴的相关记录。罗伊将担任我此项研究以及今后实验报告的助手。
初秋 10 日：

entries.en: Today the mage association hauled an undead organism into the lab, and I was given a brief description of what it was doing in the Catacombs. Unfortunately, I was not present during the capture process.
entries.zh: 今天法师协会把一个不死生物拖进了实验室，我听取了它在地下墓穴中活动情况的简要说明。遗憾的是，捕获过程我并不在场。

entries.en: The creature matches most historical descriptions of undead humans known as Zombies. This specimen resembles an old female, seeming to have originally died from old age. We christened the newly discovered Zombie, New.
entries.zh: 这个生物与历史上对被称为“僵尸”的不死人类的描述大体一致。该样本看上去是一位老年女性，最初似乎是寿终正寝。我们给这只新发现的僵尸取名为“新”。

entries.en: New is the first Zombie seen and recorded in over 400 years, when the infamous Kaeman returned to the Castle. When compared to previous records of Zombies, we found striking similarities, just as we theorized. They only care for human flesh.
entries.zh: “新”是四百多年来第一只被发现并记录在案的僵尸，上一次还是臭名昭著的凯曼回到城堡的时候。与以往的僵尸记录对比后，我们发现了惊人的相似之处，正如我们所推测的那样：它们只对人类的血肉感兴趣。

entries.en: Upon further study we have discovered that the traits of New are as follows; Simple wounds are patched over time, although its process of rotting seems to be natural. They also have a sense for humans that are within their vicinity.
entries.zh: 经过进一步研究，我们发现“新”具有以下特征：简单的伤口会随时间愈合，尽管其腐烂过程看起来是自然的。它们还能感知到附近的人类。

entries.en: During our daily necropsy, we realized that its tissues are regenerating faster than before. In light of this evolution we have to take our testing to the next stage - fresh human corpses.
entries.zh: 在每日的尸检中，我们发现它的组织再生速度比之前更快了。鉴于这种进化，我们必须把实验推进到下一阶段——新鲜的人类尸体。
秋季 6 日：

entries.en: New gave birth to another Zombie. We named the newborn Two. While it is still unclear how the contagion spreads, this alarming discovery raises multiple questions. These answers can only be found in the Catacombs.
entries.zh: “新”生下了另一只僵尸。我们给这只新生的僵尸取名为“二”。虽然还不清楚这种传染是如何扩散的，但这个令人不安的发现引出了许多疑问。这些答案只能在地下墓穴中找到。

entries.en: Two is far too powerful. We have failed to curb its vicious tendencies. Officer Roy was found dead in the testing facility, ripped limb from limb.
entries.zh: “二”太过强大了。我们没能遏制它凶残的本性。罗伊警官被发现死在测试设施里，尸体被撕得四分五裂。
两只僵尸现已被消灭。
远征记 第 1 卷

entries.en: "Very well." The King grasped his scepter and spoke resolutely. "I shall send a garrison of highly trained militia to further investigate the Catacombs. If dark magic is at work there, we will take care of it swiftly."
entries.zh: “很好。”国王握住权杖，语气坚决，“我将派出一支训练有素的民兵队伍，进一步调查地下墓穴。如果那里真有黑暗魔法作祟，我们会迅速处理掉它。”

entries.en: The atmosphere in the room became more serious but the court seemed relieved. Rumors were spreading in the Kingdom concerning the living corpse found in the crypts, and after the tragedy in the facility, people's mindsets started to worsen.
entries.zh: 房间里的气氛变得更加凝重，但朝臣们似乎松了口气。墓穴里发现会动的尸体的传闻正在王国中蔓延，而在研究设施的惨剧之后，人心越发惶惶。

entries.en: General Dan would lead the expedition, accompanied by Solomon. The King believed that sending a mage from his personal guard would appease the villagers. Once again this subterfuge was seen through by the court members.
entries.zh: 远征将由丹将军率领，所罗门随行。国王认为，派出一名他的近卫法师可以安抚村民。这次的障眼法又一次被朝臣们看穿了。

entries.en: At nightfall, the garrison had gathered enough resources for at least 5 days of traveling, but only the bare minimum of necessities. The group of 50 soldiers and 3 mages would take their leave in the morning, right as the rooster crows.
entries.zh: 到了傍晚，队伍已备齐了至少五天行程所需的物资，但只带了最基本的必需品。这支由 50 名士兵和 3 名法师组成的队伍，将在第二天清晨鸡鸣时出发。
诡异的遗骸

entries.en: We entered the Catacombs. I still have no idea what we are looking for in this death hole, nobody tells me much anyways. After all, in the army, I'm at the bottom of the food chain.
entries.zh: 我们进入了地下墓穴。我到现在都不知道我们要在这个死人窟里找什么，反正也没人跟我多说。毕竟在军队里，我处在食物链的最底层。

entries.en: Before entering this giant graveyard, I couldn't believe any of the stories. But now that I'm here, I'm not sure what to think anymore. This place is darker than a moonless night, everything is tainted with shadows.
entries.zh: 进入这座巨大的墓地之前，那些传说我一个都不信。可现在身在其中，我也不知道该怎么想了。这里比没有月亮的夜晚还要黑，一切都笼罩在阴影里。

entries.en: Everywhere I look I see stone and dust. I don't want to be buried in a forgotten place like this. Now that I think of it, most of those people were probably soldiers like me, or what remains of them.
entries.zh: 放眼望去，到处都是石头和灰尘。我可不想被埋在这种被遗忘的地方。现在想想，这里埋的大多数人，大概都是像我这样的士兵，或者说是他们剩下的部分。

entries.en: Tens of thousands died on that fateful day, this place probably took years to build. I hear people whisper about the Wither King...nonsense. Fables and legends are for songs, there is only blood and steel.
entries.zh: 那个命中注定的日子里死了成千上万的人，这个地方恐怕花了好几年才建成。我听见有人在窃窃私语，说什么凋灵之王……胡扯。寓言和传说是拿来唱的，这世上只有鲜血和钢铁。

entries.en: We were almost through with the first floor when one of the young recruits screamed. In his hysteria, I heard him mention a talking skull. Can't blame the poor lad, those skulls seem to look at you all the time.
entries.zh: 第一层快走完的时候，一个年轻的新兵尖叫起来。在他歇斯底里的叫喊中，我听到他提到了一颗会说话的头骨。也不能怪这可怜的小伙子，那些头骨好像一直都在盯着你看。

entries.en: "It's warning us..." he murmured. If there is one thing that I know for sure, those little tricks won't work on the sergeant. I've had my fair share of insubordination, already learned that lesson ten times over.
entries.zh: “它在警告我们……”他喃喃道。有一件事我很确定，这种小把戏对中士可不管用。不服从命令的苦头我吃得够多了，这个教训我已经学过十遍了。

entries.en: Still, that look of fear in his eyes, it seemed so real... This kid is creeping me out. In fact, the whole place is giving me goosebumps. Did that skull just turn towards me? Those shadows are deceiving me.
entries.zh: 可他眼中的那种恐惧，看起来那么真实……这孩子让我心里发毛。说实话，整个地方都让我起鸡皮疙瘩。那颗头骨刚才是不是转向了我？是那些阴影在骗我。

entries.en: Halfway through the second floor, one of the scouts noticed an irregularity. We followed him through a corridor which opened into a large crypt. The tombs kept inside all seemed broken as if the whole place had been looted.
entries.zh: 第二层走到一半时，一名斥候发现了异常。我们跟着他穿过一条走廊，来到一间巨大的墓室。里面的坟墓似乎全都被砸开了，就好像整个地方都被洗劫过一样。

entries.en: Solomon asked for all the soldiers to stay outside of the room, and then called the rest to inspect the crypt. After what felt like half an hour, the mages and scientists gathered around General Dan and the King's mage.
entries.zh: 所罗门要求所有士兵留在房间外面，然后叫其他人进去检查墓室。感觉过了大约半个小时，法师和科学家们聚到了丹将军和国王的法师身边。

entries.en: There was no trace of any remains, the bodies and anything else those tombs used to protect were gone. This development corroborates the suspicions of evil work in the Catacombs, the expedition must press on.
entries.zh: 墓里没有任何遗骸的痕迹，尸体以及那些坟墓原本守护的一切都不见了。这一发现印证了地下墓穴中有邪恶活动的怀疑，远征必须继续。

entries.en: Whoever took those corpses left no clues behind. There are signs of human activity, but all those trails and footsteps lead to nowhere, just as if they walked right through the walls.
entries.zh: 不管是谁带走了那些尸体，都没留下任何线索。这里有人类活动的迹象，但所有的痕迹和脚印都通向死路，就像他们直接穿墙而过了一样。

entries.en: After nearly 16 hours, it was time to rest. Because the crypt was large enough and had just been inspected, General Dan ordered the men to gather inside and spend the night.
entries.zh: 走了将近 16 个小时，该休息了。由于这间墓室足够大，又刚刚检查过，丹将军命令士兵们都聚到里面过夜。
严峻的逆境

entries.en: A scream broke the silence of the night. It came from right next to me, maybe 3 meters, no, less. My first instinct was to look for my sword first and think later. My mind was still blurred from waking up, and my eyes could barely see.
entries.zh: 一声尖叫划破了夜晚的寂静。声音就在我身边，大概 3 米，不，更近。我的第一反应是先找到剑，再想别的。我刚醒，脑子还是一片混沌，眼睛几乎什么也看不清。

entries.en: That scream again, full of terror. My fingers grabbed onto a familiar handle. I turned my head towards the sound and raised my sword in front of me, voices echoing from the rest of the room.
entries.zh: 又是那声尖叫，充满了恐惧。我的手指摸到了一个熟悉的剑柄。我把头转向声音传来的方向，在身前举起剑，房间其他地方传来阵阵人声。

entries.en: Albert was there, frantically trying to grab onto something. He's trying to crawl, or so I thought. I realized that Albert's hand was covered with blood, his fingernails making an atrocious sound on the ground.
entries.zh: 艾伯特就在那里，拼命想抓住什么东西。我以为他是想往前爬。接着我才发现，艾伯特的手上满是鲜血，他的指甲在地上刮出刺耳的声响。

entries.en: I could sense a dark mass behind him, a man. "ALBERT!" I screamed as I lunged forward. My blade pierced through the assassin, and as I got closer, a light revealed my enemy. Visions of horror.
entries.zh: 我感觉到他身后有一团黑影，是个人。“艾伯特！”我大喊一声扑了上去。我的剑刺穿了那个刺客，等我靠近时，一道光照出了我的敌人。那是恐怖的景象。

entries.en: No eyes, and barely any skin. The face of death. My heart paced to a crawl, I couldn't move. Its rotten hand grabbed my arm and started to crush it like a twig. The pain brought me back to reality. I screamed and tried to free my arm.
entries.zh: 没有眼睛，几乎没有皮肤。那是死亡的面孔。我的心跳几乎停滞，整个人动弹不得。它那腐烂的手抓住我的胳膊，像捏一根树枝一样开始用力。剧痛把我拉回了现实。我尖叫着想把胳膊抽出来。

entries.en: The creature held on to it, but I kept pulling with everything I had. During the struggle I fell on my back, the thing lying over me. Something warm dropped from its jaw onto my neck, blood and flesh. Albert, or some of him.
entries.zh: 那东西死死抓着不放，我用尽全身力气往回拽。挣扎中我仰面摔倒，那东西压在我身上。有什么温热的东西从它的下巴滴到我的脖子上，是血和肉。是艾伯特，或者说他的一部分。

entries.en: There was an explosion of light, I closed my eyes. A weight got taken off of me, moments later I understood why. A spell landed on the creature, tearing it apart. The fiend flew across the room and landed behind Albert.
entries.zh: 一道强光炸开，我闭上了眼睛。压在身上的重量消失了，过了一会儿我才明白是怎么回事。一道法术击中了那个怪物，把它撕成了碎片。那恶魔飞过房间，落在了艾伯特身后。

entries.en: Something cracked in my arm, the hand of the beast was still pressuring it with inhuman strength. I managed to grab the thumb and freed myself from its grip.
entries.zh: 我的胳膊里有什么东西断了，那怪物的手仍以非人的力气紧紧攥着。我设法掰住它的拇指，挣脱了它的手。

entries.en: The hand landed on the ground and kept moving towards me.
entries.zh: 那只手掉在地上，还在不停地朝我爬过来。

entries.en: Another lightning strike, the hand stopped. Solomon was standing next to me, holding my shoulder. His lips moved but I couldn't hear him, he was pointing at my arm. I turned my head in the direction of Albert, but he was dead...
entries.zh: 又是一道闪电，那只手不动了。所罗门站在我旁边，扶着我的肩膀。他的嘴唇在动，可我听不见他在说什么，他指着我的胳膊。我把头转向艾伯特那边，但他已经死了……

entries.en: A zombie attacked our group during the night, killing one soldier and breaking the arm of another. The 2 guards on shift were standing in front of the only entrance to the room, and swore that nothing came from that corridor.
entries.zh: 夜里一只僵尸袭击了我们的队伍，杀死了一名士兵，还折断了另一名士兵的胳膊。当班的两名守卫一直站在房间唯一的入口前，他们发誓没有任何东西从那条走廊进来过。

entries.en: Somehow that zombie ended up on the opposite side of the Crypt that we thoroughly investigated only hours before. What is even more concerning, is what it did to those soldiers.
entries.zh: 不知怎么的，那只僵尸出现在了墓室的另一头，而那里我们几个小时前才彻底检查过。更令人担忧的，是它对那些士兵做的事。

entries.en: It first planted its teeth in the skull of one of the soldiers and took a large bite out of his brain. How Albert survived for so long is a mystery in and of itself. As a precaution, we burned his body.
entries.zh: 它先是把牙齿咬进一名士兵的头骨，从他的脑子上咬下了一大块。艾伯特怎么能撑那么久，本身就是个谜。为保险起见，我们烧掉了他的尸体。

entries.en: Even after losing limbs, the detached body parts kept operating on their own until the brain was destroyed. Our current theory is that the amygdala has to be intact for the zombie to function.
entries.zh: 即使断了肢，脱落的身体部位在大脑被摧毁之前仍会自行活动。我们目前的推测是，僵尸要想活动，杏仁核必须完好无损。

entries.en: Solomon noticed fluid on the chainmail of the other soldier, where the hand grabbed his arm. It can hardly be described without deeper analysis. This liquid could be a clue to those transformations or even the cause.
entries.zh: 所罗门在另一名士兵的锁子甲上发现了一种液体，就在那只手抓住他胳膊的地方。不经过深入分析，很难描述它是什么。这种液体可能是这些转变的线索，甚至就是其原因。

entries.en: The expedition left the room less than an hour after the incident. The group was reaching the end of the second floor when we got confronted by another apparition, the new creature killing 3 of our men before getting taken down.
entries.zh: 事发后不到一个小时，远征队就离开了那个房间。队伍快走到第二层尽头时，又遭遇了另一个怪物，这个新出现的生物在被击倒之前杀死了我们 3 个人。

entries.en: No doubt the undead we found was a Wither Skeleton, the same creatures that were described attacking the castle centuries ago, led by Kaeman, the self-proclaimed "Wither King."
entries.zh: 毫无疑问，我们遇到的这个不死生物是凋灵骷髅，和几个世纪前在自封为“凋灵之王”的凯曼率领下进攻城堡的那些怪物是同一种。

entries.en: Skeletons, dark as the night, overbearing in nature, with bones akin to onyx, seemingly fragile but as tough as steel. This one was holding a stone sword and was strong enough to cut through a man wearing full armor with a single swing.
entries.zh: 这些骷髅漆黑如夜，气势逼人，骨头像缟玛瑙一样，看似脆弱却坚硬如钢。这一只手持石剑，力量大得一剑就能把穿着全套盔甲的人劈成两半。

entries.en: Solomon believes that the Expedition must return to the King's Castle at once, we have reason to believe that Kaeman survived and took hold of the Catacombs. Our group isn't prepared for a confrontation with the Wither King.
entries.zh: 所罗门认为远征队必须立刻返回国王的城堡，我们有理由相信凯曼还活着，并且已经占据了地下墓穴。我们的队伍还没准备好与凋灵之王正面交锋。

entries.en: General Dan ordered the troops to march on, insisting that we at least explore the third floor before turning back. After all, we still had enough resources for another 4 days of travel.
entries.zh: 丹将军命令部队继续前进，坚持至少要探索完第三层再回头。毕竟，我们的物资还够再走 4 天。

entries.en: Before our encounter with the Wither Skeleton, we heard plenty of odd noises. But during our time on the third floor, just like the first one, there was a deafening silence that caused great anxiety in us all.
entries.zh: 在遭遇凋灵骷髅之前，我们听到过许多古怪的声响。可在第三层的这段时间里，就像在第一层时一样，四周一片死寂，让我们所有人都焦虑不已。

entries.en: After a few hours, the group entered a large room, probably the largest one yet. The room had giant water pipes landing into large pools. Proof that the sewers had connections with the Catacombs.
entries.zh: 几个小时后，队伍进入一个大房间，可能是目前为止最大的一个。房间里有巨大的水管，一直通到几个大水池里。这证明下水道与地下墓穴是相通的。

entries.en: The General said it was time for a break, so the group started to prepare for lunch. Solomon reiterated his wish to return to the Castle immediately. After a short debate, General Dan agreed to end the expedition.
entries.zh: 将军说该休息了，于是大家开始准备午饭。所罗门再次表示希望立刻返回城堡。经过短暂的争论，丹将军同意结束远征。

entries.en: Suddenly, someone yelled that enemies were coming. The sounds grew louder and louder, before encompassing us completely. We were surrounded, hundreds of those creatures, how could they be capable of such coordination?
entries.zh: 突然，有人大喊敌人来了。声音越来越响，最后将我们完全包围。我们被包围了，成百上千只那种怪物，它们怎么能配合得如此默契？

entries.en: Giant spiders crawled out of the sewers, zombies appeared from the hall, and a volley of skeletons came from the other direction. The General immediately called for a rally and a desperate battle ensued.
entries.zh: 巨型蜘蛛从下水道里爬了出来，僵尸从大厅里涌现，另一个方向则冲来一大群骷髅。将军立即召集众人，一场绝望的战斗爆发了。

entries.en: Somewhere in the chaos, I saw an opportunity to retreat. I landed a stun spell on a group of enemies near the entrance of the hall and quickly made my escape. A small portion of our group followed me into the passage.
entries.zh: 混乱之中，我看到了一个撤退的机会。我对大厅入口附近的一群敌人施放了一道眩晕法术，迅速逃了出去。队伍里有一小部分人跟着我进了通道。

entries.en: I do not know what happened to Solomon, the General, and the rest of the militia. I found refuge with a couple soldiers far away from the battle, but I could sense a presence watching us.
entries.zh: 我不知道所罗门、将军和其他民兵后来怎么样了。我和几名士兵在远离战场的地方找到了藏身之处，但我能感觉到，有什么东西在注视着我们。

entries.en: One of the rescued soldiers was acting odd. He started mumbling to himself, and knowing the Catacombs, I was ready for whatever this could be. He started screaming "GET OUT!!!", and clawed at his eyes. Then, he stopped.
entries.zh: 被救下的士兵中有一个举止古怪。他开始自言自语，我了解地下墓穴，所以已做好了应对任何情况的准备。他开始尖叫“滚出去！！！”，还用手抓自己的眼睛。然后，他停了下来。

entries.en: Suddenly, he leaped at his comrade and tried to pierce him with his sword. I used all the mana I had left to stun him before he could kill. The color in his eyes was gone, as if he was being mind controlled.
entries.zh: 突然，他扑向自己的战友，想用剑刺穿对方。我用尽剩下的全部法力，在他下手之前把他击晕了。他眼中的颜色消失了，就好像被人控制了心智一样。
[缺失的一页]

entries.en: The Catacombs hide an entire army of incredible strength. Someone has to come back alive from the expedition at all c...
entries.zh: 地下墓穴里藏着一整支实力惊人的军队。无论付出什么代价，远征队里都必须有人活着回去……
墙壁

entries.en: I saw it all. Monsters everywhere and every kind, in an instant chaos reigned over the room. We were all in battle formation around Dan, pretending to be in control, everyone was scared for their lives.
entries.zh: 我全都看见了。到处都是怪物，各式各样，转眼间整个房间就陷入了混乱。我们都围在丹的身边列好战斗阵形，装作一切尽在掌握，其实每个人都怕得要命。

entries.en: I fought alongside Dan many times, the man is a legend, but how foolish can he be? Nobody in the group comes even close to his skills, we are all fodder to those foes. We should have tried to escape instead of fighting.
entries.zh: 我和丹并肩作战过很多次，这个人是个传奇，可他怎么能这么愚蠢？队伍里没有一个人的本事能跟他相提并论，在这些敌人面前我们全都是炮灰。我们本该设法逃跑，而不是在这里拼命。

entries.en: The army of undead ran straight at us. "Their brains, aim for their brains!" someone yelled in the back. How can I aim for the brain of a skeleton that doesn't have one? This magic is beyond anything that they know.
entries.zh: 不死大军径直朝我们冲来。“它们的脑子，瞄准它们的脑子！”后面有人喊道。可骷髅根本没有脑子，我怎么瞄准？这种魔法远远超出了他们的认知。

entries.en: The sound of swords slicing through bloodless corpses, almost like chopping down wood. Zombies are terrifyingly strong but most of them have no equipment, nor technique, just fearlessly running to their end.
entries.zh: 剑刃劈开没有血的尸体，声音就像在砍木头。僵尸力大无穷，令人胆寒，但大多数都没有装备，也不懂招式，只是毫无畏惧地奔向自己的末路。

entries.en: I think it was Solomon's spells slowing them all, their movements seemed sluggish, compared to when they entered the room. The mage looked exhausted already, his face contorted by the concentration.
entries.zh: 我想是所罗门的法术让它们都慢了下来，和刚进房间时相比，它们的动作显得迟缓了许多。这位法师看上去已经精疲力竭，脸因为全神贯注而扭曲。

entries.en: More and more came, it seemed endless. I saw a mage escape with a few soldiers, I wonder what happened to them. And then, it happened. The battle was raging when another of those giant black skeletons entered the room.
entries.zh: 敌人越来越多，好像永无止境。我看见一名法师带着几个士兵逃走了，不知道他们后来怎么样了。然后，那件事发生了。战斗正酣时，又一只巨大的黑色骷髅走进了房间。

entries.en: The obsidian-looking creature ran straight at the General, who had noticed it.
entries.zh: 这个看起来像黑曜石一样的怪物径直冲向将军，而将军也注意到了它。

entries.en: Dan faced towards it with all his might, the battle veteran was even bigger than the skeleton. He raised his two-handed sword and held it above his head.
entries.zh: 丹用尽全力迎了上去，这位身经百战的老兵甚至比那骷髅还要高大。他举起双手大剑，高高擎过头顶。

entries.en: It was over in an instant. The skeleton was wicked fast. I held my breath almost as if I was bracing for impact. Dan's massive sword cut through the air incredibly swiftly, breaking the enemy's sword in half and the skeleton with it.
entries.zh: 一切在瞬间结束。那骷髅快得吓人。我屏住呼吸，几乎像在准备承受冲击。丹的巨剑以不可思议的速度划破空气，把敌人的剑连同骷髅一起劈成了两半。

entries.en: We finally had hope, if anyone could get us out of here alive, it was General Dan. After defeating the Wither Skeleton, the colossal soldier turned towards the rest of the forces and released a battle cry, we all responded.
entries.zh: 我们终于有了希望，如果有谁能带我们活着离开这里，那就是丹将军。击败凋灵骷髅后，这位巨人般的战士转向其余的部队，发出一声战吼，我们全都高声回应。

entries.en: Coming out of his apparent torpor, Solomon spoke. "Something is coming... We need to get out of here!" The mage started running towards one of the entrances. "Dan! We have to!" I looked towards the other entrance, and I saw it.
entries.zh: 所罗门从看似恍惚的状态中回过神来，开口说道：“有东西要来了……我们得离开这里！”这位法师开始朝其中一个入口跑去。“丹！我们必须走！”我朝另一个入口望去，看见了它。

entries.en: The nightmare creature entered the room, it looked half human and half wither skeleton, with multiple heads. It levitated over the corpses and in an awful scream, threw a dark spell right through the General. It was over.
entries.zh: 那个噩梦般的生物走进了房间，它看起来一半是人，一半是凋灵骷髅，长着好几个头。它悬浮在尸体上方，发出一声可怕的尖啸，射出一道黑暗法术，直接贯穿了将军。一切都结束了。

entries.en: Whoever was left from the expedition started running in total disarray. I followed Solomon, who turned just in time to create a magic barrier, protecting us from more of those demonic spells.
entries.zh: 远征队剩下的人四散奔逃，乱作一团。我跟着所罗门，他及时转身筑起一道魔法屏障，保护我们免受更多恶魔法术的攻击。

entries.en: I don't know what happened to Solomon, my only concern was with getting as far away as possible. Further in the corridor I saw a dead soldier, who probably escaped earlier. He was holding a torch and other materials, I would need them.
entries.zh: 我不知道所罗门后来怎么样了，我唯一在乎的就是逃得越远越好。在走廊深处，我看到一具士兵的尸体，大概是之前逃出来的。他手里拿着火把和其他物资，我会用得上。

entries.en: Eventually, hours after I escaped the undead horde, I came upon a room full of empty tombs, and that's where I decided to take shelter for the night. I moved some pillars to block the doorway to prevent things from sneaking inside.
entries.zh: 逃离不死大军几个小时后，我终于来到一个满是空坟的房间，决定在那里过夜。我挪了几根柱子堵住门口，免得有东西偷偷溜进来。

entries.en: The next morning, everything had gone a lot smoother than expected, nothing came for me while I was resting. No signs of the expedition either, but I had to stay quiet if I wanted to escape this place alive.
entries.zh: 第二天早上，一切比预想的顺利得多，我休息时什么也没来找我。也没有远征队的任何踪迹，但如果我想活着离开这里，就必须保持安静。

entries.en: I walked through hours on end. It was impossible to find the entrance of the third floor, so I took a short rest. With an excess of coal on my hands, I decided I would draw markings on the walls, to identify where I had been previously.
entries.zh: 我走了一个又一个小时。根本找不到第三层的入口，于是我稍作休息。手上的煤炭多得用不完，我决定在墙上画记号，标出我去过的地方。

entries.en: When I left the tomb area earlier, something seemed off. I was almost certain there was a dead end to the left of the hall, but now it's opened up. Did it collapse during the night, or am I going crazy?
entries.zh: 早些时候离开坟墓区时，我就觉得有点不对劲。我几乎可以肯定大厅左边是一条死路，可现在却通了。是夜里塌开的，还是我疯了？

entries.en: After hours of exploring, and charting out a basic map, I returned to my previous resting place by following the coal lines drawn upon the floor and walls. However, when I made it back the room was no longer there.
entries.zh: 探索了几个小时，画出一张简单的地图后，我顺着画在地面和墙上的煤炭线回到之前休息的地方。可等我回去时，那个房间已经不在那里了。

entries.en: I walked off to the left side of the corridor, would my mark still be present? Everything was fine, I noticed the opening was there, it was not a dead end. But as I followed my marking, it was cut off rather abruptly.
entries.zh: 我走到走廊左侧，我的记号还在吗？一切正常，我看到那个开口还在，那里不是死路。可当我顺着记号走时，它却戛然而止。

entries.en: There was no smearing on the ground, it was as if the stain was peeled off. It looked completely unnatural. As I walked further, I cast my gaze to the ceiling. There was a black streak, looking directly into my eyes.
entries.zh: 地上没有任何擦抹的痕迹，就好像那道印记是被整个揭掉了一样。这看起来完全不自然。我继续往前走，抬头望向天花板。那里有一道黑色的线，正直直地盯着我的眼睛。

entries.en: There was no mistaking it, it was the one I had drawn, but it was now on the ceiling? It was as if this place was... moving? My Lord... How is this even possible? I have to find a way, I have to...
entries.zh: 不会错的，那就是我画的那一道，可它现在怎么会在天花板上？就好像这个地方……在移动？我的天……这怎么可能？我必须找到办法，我必须……

entries.en: Are these walls alive? Who's doing this? What a terrible joke, why don't you come out and kill me already? I don't even have food or anything to drink. GET IT OVER WITH! DON'T YOU SEE?! I'M AS GOOD AS DEAD!!!
entries.zh: 这些墙是活的吗？是谁在搞鬼？多么可怕的玩笑，你为什么不干脆出来杀了我？我连吃的喝的都没有。快点结束吧！你没看见吗？！我已经跟死人没两样了！！！

entries.en: As I walked past the walls, I could hear a faint cry, and now, every time I looked at them, they stared back at me. It's as if they were made from the souls of people! I'll die right here, and maybe I'll join them.
entries.zh: 从墙边走过时，我能听到微弱的哭声，而现在，每次我看向它们，它们都会回瞪着我。就好像它们是用人的灵魂做成的！我会死在这里，也许我会加入它们。

entries.en: All I have left is coal... Yes, all I have, coal. coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal, coal
entries.zh: 我只剩下煤炭了……对，我只有煤炭了。煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭，煤炭
眼睛

entries.en: The first time I saw it was on the first floor, a large floating eye. Nobody else noticed. It was looking straight at me. I didn't tell anyone, but I know what I saw, that thing isn't human, but it didn't seem like an enemy.
entries.zh: 我第一次看到它是在第一层，一只悬浮在空中的巨大眼睛。其他人都没注意到。它正直勾勾地盯着我。我没告诉任何人，但我知道自己看到了什么，那东西不是人，但它似乎也不是敌人。

entries.en: It appeared again on the second floor, twice. Again, I was the only one who saw. It seemed interested only with me. I can tell when it is watching, there is a strange sensation in my head when it happens, and I know exactly where to look.
entries.zh: 它在第二层又出现了两次。这一次还是只有我看见。它好像只对我感兴趣。它在注视我时我能感觉得到，那时我的脑袋里会有一种奇怪的感觉，而且我清楚地知道该往哪里看。

entries.en: At this point I am fairly certain it was trying to communicate. Nonetheless it completely vanished after those 3 encounters. But something else happened during the battle on the third floor. I felt a different sensation..
entries.zh: 到了这时，我几乎可以肯定它是在尝试与我沟通。不过，在那 3 次相遇之后，它就彻底消失了。但在第三层的战斗中，又发生了另一件事。我感觉到了一种不同的感觉……

entries.en: Even before the Wither Skeleton appeared, I sensed a powerful spirit, long before Solomon noticed it. Was he too absorbed by his spells? How could I perceive it faster than a mage, especially one of the caliber of Solomon?
entries.zh: 早在凋灵骷髅出现之前，我就感觉到了一个强大的灵体，比所罗门察觉到还要早得多。是他太专注于施法了吗？我怎么会比一名法师更早察觉，尤其是所罗门这种级别的法师？

entries.en: Later, I escaped away from the battle, but quickly the original feeling came back. It was watching me again. I pulled my sword and turned towards it. "What do you want from me?" It came out of the shadows, the watcher.
entries.zh: 后来，我逃离了战斗，可很快那种最初的感觉又回来了。它又在注视我了。我拔出剑，转身面对它。“你想从我这里得到什么？”它从阴影中现身，那个观察者。

entries.en: So much power coming from this eye, I could almost touch it. It was far too strong for me to handle.
entries.zh: 这只眼睛散发出如此强大的力量，我几乎能触摸到它。它强大得远非我能应付。

entries.en: - What are you? Why are you following me?
entries.zh: ——你是什么东西？为什么跟着我？
——特别。

entries.en: The loud voice echoed in my head, it wasn't coming from my consciousness.
entries.zh: 那响亮的声音在我脑中回荡，那不是出自我自己的意识。

entries.en: - I'm special? What do you mean?
entries.zh: ——我很特别？你什么意思？
——你的心智……难以读取。
——读取……我的心智？
——你的名字。

entries.en: - What, why do you want to know?
entries.zh: ——什么，你为什么想知道？
——你的父母，他们是谁？

entries.en: - I... I never knew them, why are you asking this?!
entries.zh: ——我……我从来不认识他们，你为什么要问这个？！

entries.en: It asked for my name again.
entries.zh: 它又问了一遍我的名字。

entries.en: As it got closer, I could feel its presence intensify.
entries.zh: 随着它越来越近，我能感觉到它的存在感越发强烈。

entries.en: - GET OUT OF MY HEAD, I'LL KILL YOU!
entries.zh: ——滚出我的脑袋，我会杀了你！

entries.en: My sword was heavy, and my knees were weak, the world collapsed on me as I fell. I could still hear the voice.
entries.zh: 我的剑越来越沉，膝盖发软，倒下时整个世界都朝我塌了下来。我仍能听到那个声音。

entries.en: -So your name is Sadan, I see...
entries.zh: ——原来你的名字叫萨丹，我明白了……
余波

entries.en: We completely defeated the humans on the third floor. I would have eradicated them myself if Necron hadn't made an appearance. It shows how important it is for him that we stay hidden for as long as possible.
entries.zh: 我们在第三层彻底击败了那些人类。要不是耐克伦现身，我早就亲手把他们全部铲除了。这说明对他来说，让我们尽可能长久地隐藏起来有多么重要。

entries.en: I don't understand, do they think our army is still too weak? Why do they want to hide our presence for so long, we could rule over the humans on this side of the world, instead of... rotting down here.
entries.zh: 我不明白，他们觉得我们的军队还太弱吗？他们为什么要把我们的存在隐藏这么久，我们本可以统治世界这一边的人类，而不是……在这下面腐烂。

entries.en: We still don't know what caused this group of humans to explore the Catacombs, but now it is clear they had suspicions of what was inside. No matter what, we have to make a move, I think the plan is to send Storm after the Castle if they flee.
entries.zh: 我们仍不知道是什么促使这群人类来探索地下墓穴，但现在很清楚，他们已经怀疑这里面有什么了。无论如何，我们必须采取行动，我想计划是如果他们逃跑，就派斯托姆去追击城堡。

entries.en: At least I got confirmation that none of them escaped the Catacombs, and their group only had a few days worth of resources, the Kingdom will understand soon enough what happened. We must strike before they realize.
entries.zh: 至少我得到确认，他们没有一个人逃出地下墓穴，而且他们的队伍只带了几天的物资，王国很快就会明白发生了什么。我们必须在他们察觉之前发动攻击。

entries.en: Only 2 humans are left alive. It seems like Necron wanted to interrogate the mage, and the other one, I have no idea what the 'stalker' wants to do with him.
entries.zh: 只剩下 2 个人类还活着。耐克伦似乎想审问那名法师，至于另一个，我完全不知道那个“跟踪者”想拿他做什么。

entries.en: Necron is very fond of that eye, so it's free to do whatever eccentricity it wants.
entries.zh: 耐克伦很喜欢那只眼睛，所以它想怎么胡闹都随它。
学徒

entries.en: A gust of wind blew by a man with dark hair and eyes, who was walking away from the Academy's building. Necron looked terribly angry. Heated conversations with his professors were common, but after this one his mind was boiling.
entries.zh: 一阵风吹过一个黑发黑眸的男人，他正从学院的大楼里走出来。耐克伦看起来怒不可遏。和教授们激烈争吵对他来说是家常便饭，但这一次之后，他的心里怒火翻腾。

entries.en: "How dare they, how dare they threaten to expel me from the Academy! They should know all too well, I can't... I need to know what kind of magic killed my parents, all those people! 17 years went by and they still didn't change their minds."
entries.zh: “他们怎么敢，怎么敢威胁要把我赶出学院！他们心里应该再清楚不过，我不能……我必须知道是什么样的魔法杀死了我的父母，杀死了那么多人！17 年过去了，他们还是不肯改变主意。”

entries.en: "The worst student they said! Then why don't they help me instead, I can feel my potential growing, I can sense mana all around me, I was born to be a mage. I just need... something. Even I can't describe what exactly I'm lacking."
entries.zh: “说我是最差的学生！那他们为什么不来帮我？我能感觉到自己的潜力在增长，我能感知到周围的法力，我生来就该成为法师。我只是需要……某种东西。就连我自己也说不清到底缺了什么。”

entries.en: "It is almost as if I can hear mana and understand it, but I can't speak its language. Yes, that's it! It speaks to me but I can't 'answer' it back, or not well enough, at least for now." He stopped walking as he said that.
entries.zh: “就好像我能听见法力、理解法力，却说不出它的语言。没错，就是这样！它在跟我说话，我却没法‘回应’它，或者说回应得不够好，至少现在还不行。”说着，他停下了脚步。

entries.en: "But if they expel me, where will I go? I have nothing, if only... If only they could trust me, I need to read those scrolls, it is vital. I am drawn to them, every day that goes by makes it even more clear, the answer to all my problems."
entries.zh: “可如果他们把我赶出去，我能去哪儿？我一无所有，要是……要是他们能信任我就好了，我必须读到那些卷轴，这至关重要。我被它们吸引着，日子每过一天，我就越清楚，那是我所有问题的答案。”

entries.en: "If I could open a single scroll, I would instantly realize. But I already know, maybe I've always known. That forbidden magic, what is locked and labelled as taboo, THAT is my language. I will reveal it to the world, and save them all."
entries.zh: “只要能打开一份卷轴，我立刻就会明白。但我其实已经知道了，也许我一直都知道。那种被锁起来、被列为禁忌的禁忌魔法，那才是我的语言。我要把它公之于世，拯救所有人。”
追随者

entries.en: Another vision, like usual it felt like someone else was controlling it. From there he could see the castle, but in shambles, like if centuries had passed. Most visions appeared from a different time, where the world is more advanced.
entries.zh: 又一个幻象，和往常一样，感觉像是有别人在操控它。从那里他能看见城堡，但已是一片废墟，仿佛过了好几个世纪。大多数幻象都来自另一个时代，那里的世界更加先进。

entries.en: The vision took him down the mountain, all the way down, a large portal was standing there on the ground, he had seen it before in another vision. Standing next to it, a group of adventurers he also had seen before, years ago.
entries.zh: 幻象带着他走下山，一直走到山脚，那里的地面上立着一座巨大的传送门，他在另一个幻象中见过它。站在传送门旁边的，是一群他多年前也曾见过的冒险者。
——“拉斯罗普……拉斯罗普！”

entries.en: -"Y-yes Dr. Emmett?" he said as he emerged from the dream.
entries.zh: ——“是……是的，埃米特博士？”他从梦中回过神来。

entries.en: -"Lathrop, I need you to do something for me, and how many times do I have to tell you, stop idling around the breach, you are perturbing my tools!"
entries.zh: ——“拉斯罗普，我需要你帮我办件事，还有，我得跟你说多少遍，别在裂隙旁边闲逛，你会干扰我的仪器！”

entries.en: "Sorry Doctor, it's just... I saw the Eye again yesterday, the one I talked to you about."
entries.zh: “对不起，博士，只是……我昨天又看到那只眼睛了，就是我跟您说过的那只。”

entries.en: "Yes Lathrop, of course, the 'floating eye'. I'm sure that was very interesting. However, I am serious, this experiment is important, you know that."
entries.zh: “是啊，拉斯罗普，当然，那只‘漂浮的眼睛’。我相信那一定很有意思。不过我是认真的，这个实验很重要，你知道的。”

entries.en: "I need you to deliver a letter to my colleague in the wilderness, and quickly. As it is getting very late, you can spend the night at the inn after delivery. I'll give you enough money for a room and a good meal."
entries.zh: “我需要你把一封信送给我在荒野的同事，要快。天已经很晚了，送完信你可以在旅馆住一晚。我会给你足够的钱，够你开个房间、吃顿好饭。”

entries.en: "When you return, don't forget to bring back groceries and some chalk."
entries.zh: “回来的时候，别忘了买些食物和粉笔。”

entries.en: "Understood, I will be on my way then Dr. Emmett, have a good evening, and if you study on the balcony, make sure to keep yourself warm."
entries.zh: “明白，那我这就出发了，埃米特博士，祝您晚上愉快。如果您要在阳台上研究，记得保暖。”
“我会的，拉斯罗普，谢谢你。”

entries.en: Lathrop went down the ladder, entered the house to grab the letter and money the Doctor left for him and exited the house in the direction of the zipline. After a few steps, he turned around to look at the house. For some reason he felt sad.
entries.zh: 拉斯罗普爬下梯子，进屋拿上博士留给他的信和钱，然后出门朝滑索的方向走去。走了几步，他回头看了看那座房子。不知为何，他感到一阵悲伤。

entries.en: He had lived in this house his entire life. Soon after birth, the calamity made him an orphan, like many others. On that day, a magical breach got created at the top of the mountain, almost invisible to the eye.
entries.zh: 他一辈子都住在这座房子里。出生后不久，那场大灾变就让他和许多人一样成了孤儿。就在那一天，山顶上出现了一道魔法裂隙，肉眼几乎看不见。

entries.en: Soon after, Dr. Emmett started studying the breach to understand what could be across it, but never succeeded to travel through it. In over thirty years, the breach opened once, and only Lathrop noticed it, in fact, he was expecting it.
entries.zh: 不久之后，埃米特博士开始研究这道裂隙，想弄清另一边可能是什么，却始终没能穿过它。三十多年来，裂隙只打开过一次，而且只有拉斯罗普察觉到了，事实上，他早就在等着这一刻。

entries.en: Lathrop was fortunate enough to be raised by Dr. Emmett after he moved into the house of his late parents. He learned how to read and write, and met many great mages and scientists, all close friends of his adoptive father.
entries.zh: 埃米特博士搬进拉斯罗普已故父母的房子后，拉斯罗普有幸由他抚养长大。他学会了读书写字，还结识了许多伟大的法师和科学家，他们都是他养父的好友。

entries.en: For as long as he remembers, the breach showed him visions, sometimes even talked to him. At first it was vague images and colors, sometimes in his dreams. He learned to live with it, as if it was his own consciousness.
entries.zh: 从他记事起，裂隙就一直向他展示幻象，有时甚至会跟他说话。起初只是模糊的画面和色彩，有时出现在梦里。他学会了与之共存，就好像那是他自己的意识一样。

entries.en: While the doctor always acknowledged that his visions were due to the breach, their depiction by Lathrop always made them seem incoherent and therefore he couldn't draw the line between hallucinations and reality.
entries.zh: 虽然博士一直承认他的幻象是裂隙造成的，但拉斯罗普描述出来的总是显得语无伦次，因此博士无法分清哪些是幻觉，哪些是现实。

entries.en: Lately the visions were getting more vivid. The Eye appeared again in a few reveries, and with it, more frequent and detailed dreams. Unlike the usual aimless ones, those looked as part of a plan, perhaps instructions for him to follow?
entries.zh: 最近，幻象变得越来越清晰。那只眼睛又在几次遐想中出现，随之而来的是更频繁、更详细的梦。和平时那些漫无目的的梦不同，这些梦看起来像是某个计划的一部分，也许是要他照着做的指示？

entries.en: After crossing the wooden bridge, Lathrop soon reached the zipline where he began his descent to the Castle. The hour was late and he had to hurry, but he could not stop thinking of the eye and its call...
entries.zh: 走过木桥后，拉斯罗普很快来到滑索处，开始向城堡滑下去。天色已晚，他得抓紧时间，可他满脑子都是那只眼睛和它的召唤……
学徒 2

entries.en: The young man was standing on the bed by his window, his eyes lost in the canopy of the forest by the Academy. The movement of the leaves in the moonlight was mesmerizing. So much had happened lately, he couldn't sleep.
entries.zh: 年轻人站在窗边的床上，目光迷失在学院旁那片森林的树冠中。月光下树叶的摇曳令人着迷。最近发生了太多事，他睡不着。

entries.en: The hand that he had left on his grimoire started tingling. Sigh - "You really don't like me, do you?" He said as he took the old book to place it in his drawer. "It's not your fault, nor mine."
entries.zh: 他搁在魔法书上的那只手开始发麻。他叹了口气——“你是真的不喜欢我，对吧？”他一边说，一边把那本旧书放进抽屉，“这不是你的错，也不是我的错。”

entries.en: Laying on his bed his thoughts traveled to many different places. What was he going to do with all this free time? The Mage Exam was in 10 days, for the summer solstice, no amount of work would be enough to pass this test.
entries.zh: 躺在床上，他的思绪飘向了许多地方。这么多空闲时间要拿来做什么？法师考试还有 10 天，就在夏至那天，再怎么努力也不可能通过。

entries.en: Already one of the oldest students, and only capable of executing very simple spells, the only reason why he was still allowed in the Academy was that the dean of the Association took him in as his own after the tragedy that befell his parents.
entries.zh: 他已经是年纪最大的学生之一，却只会施放非常简单的法术，他之所以还能留在学院，唯一的原因是父母遭遇不幸后，协会的院长把他当作自己的孩子收养了。

entries.en: "That man..." He tightened his hand and spoke with disdain. "He thinks so highly of himself like he's some sort of father figure to me! But all he does is restrict my actions, he doesn't understand at all..."
entries.zh: “那个人……”他攥紧了手，语气轻蔑，“他把自己看得那么高，好像他是我的什么父亲一样！可他做的只是限制我的行动，他根本一点都不懂……”

entries.en: As his eyes were starting to close shut, he heard a subtle sound, the rustle of paper on the ground near the door. Someone had slid a paper below it. He could barely see from that distance, but he was getting a strange impression.
entries.zh: 就在他快要闭上眼睛时，他听到一个细微的声音，是门边地上纸张摩擦的沙沙声。有人从门缝底下塞进来一张纸。离得太远，他几乎看不清，但他有一种奇怪的感觉。

entries.en: Rushing to the door, he grabbed the item with both hands, he couldn't believe it. Instinctively he opened the door, but nobody was there, no footsteps, nothing. His heart was beating abnormally fast. Who, and how?
entries.zh: 他冲到门口，双手抓起那样东西，简直不敢相信。他本能地打开门，可外面一个人也没有，没有脚步声，什么都没有。他的心跳快得异常。是谁，又是怎么做到的？

entries.en: The scroll in his hand was bursting with magic, but not the kind his teachers were forcing him to learn. Something else, something darker... He looked around once more and went back to his room, closing the door and locking it.
entries.zh: 他手中的卷轴充盈着魔力，但不是老师们逼他学的那种。是别的东西，更黑暗的东西……他又环顾了一圈，回到房间，关上门并锁好。

entries.en: Everyone knew he was interested in those forbidden scrolls, that was no secret. Many times in the past he asked mages of the Association to make them public, arguing that we needed to understand darkness to conquer it.
entries.zh: 大家都知道他对那些禁忌卷轴感兴趣，这不是什么秘密。过去他曾多次请求协会的法师们公开它们，主张我们必须了解黑暗才能战胜黑暗。

entries.en: Forbidden Scrolls are held in the vault of the dean, protected by heavy magic spells, stealing them is unthinkable. How did anyone manage to obtain one of those, and why would they give it to him now, of all times?
entries.zh: 禁忌卷轴存放在院长的金库里，受强大的魔法咒语保护，偷走它们是不可想象的。到底是谁弄到了一份，又为什么偏偏在这个时候给他？

entries.en: He took a deep breath, trying to calm down. The spell was written with different enchanting symbols. Closing his eyes, he could still see the signs through his curtained lids. The feeling was there, the one he waited so long for.
entries.zh: 他深吸一口气，努力让自己平静下来。这个法术是用一种不同的附魔符号写成的。即使闭上眼睛，他仍能透过眼皮看到那些符号。那种感觉来了，他等待了如此之久的感觉。

entries.en: It was a simple spell, but he could learn it, he understood the mechanics and all the nuances. Mana was flowing rapidly through his body, he never felt so good, and so powerful. His eternal vocation was finally in his hands.
entries.zh: 这是个简单的法术，但他学得会，他理解其中的原理和所有细微之处。法力在他体内飞速流动，他从未感觉如此美妙、如此强大。他毕生的使命终于握在了手中。

entries.en: The dark spell could allow him to become invisible to regular magic. Quite useless he thought, but at least it was something, a confirmation of his affinity with dark magic... Maybe he could attach it to a talisman, or a ring.
entries.zh: 这个黑暗法术能让他在普通魔法面前隐形。他觉得这相当没用，但至少聊胜于无，证明了他与黑暗魔法的亲和……也许他可以把它附在一个护符或戒指上。

entries.en: What could he use it for? Invisibility essentially makes you immune to any kind of vision spell, or to enter weak barriers without notifying its creator. But there was only one barrier he knew, and that was the last place he wanted to be...
entries.zh: 他能拿它来做什么？隐形本质上能让你免疫任何探查类法术，或者在不惊动施法者的情况下进入较弱的屏障。可他只知道一道屏障，而那是他最不想去的地方……

entries.en: After only a few days, Necron had studied the scroll and learned everything about the spell, but it took him a couple more weeks to plan his next move. He could only think of one application for the spell, and it was almost too perfect.
entries.zh: 仅仅几天，耐克伦就研究完了这份卷轴，掌握了这个法术的一切，但他又花了好几周来策划下一步行动。他只能想到这个法术的一种用途，而它简直完美得过了头。

entries.en: For over a decade, after its defeat, the Wither King had been trapped in a cage on the edge of the main island. It was well guarded by mages and had a magical barrier, one that would alert the mages if someone entered.
entries.zh: 凋灵之王被击败后，十多年来一直被困在主岛边缘的一座牢笼里。那里有法师严密看守，还有一道魔法屏障，一旦有人进入就会惊动法师们。

entries.en: However, Necron could sneak through this barrier without alarming anyone, but only if he used his spell correctly. Necron's goal was to find where the Wither King is trapped inside the barrier, and question him.
entries.zh: 然而，耐克伦可以悄无声息地穿过这道屏障，前提是他正确地使用这个法术。耐克伦的目标是找到凋灵之王被困在屏障内的位置，并审问他。

entries.en: He had spent the last couple of weeks pretending to help the guards with their chores. The mages didn't really watch the cage itself, in fact, they would rather stay a reasonable distance away from it.
entries.zh: 过去几周，他一直假装帮守卫们干杂活。法师们其实并不看守牢笼本身，事实上，他们宁愿离它远远的。

entries.en: At sunset, most of the guards were off duty. Necron knew this was his time to act, so he cast his spell in a nearby forest, then proceeded to approach the barrier. Even with many precautions, he was still trembling.
entries.zh: 日落时分，大部分守卫都下了班。耐克伦知道是时候行动了，于是他在附近的森林里施放了法术，然后向屏障靠近。即使做了诸多防范，他还是在发抖。

entries.en: He had never experienced such stress in all his life, what if something went wrong? As he walked near the East cliff of the island, he quickly entered the magic barrier, and from this point on everything was a theory.
entries.zh: 他这辈子从未承受过这样的压力，万一出了差错怎么办？他走到岛的东侧悬崖附近，迅速进入了魔法屏障，从这一刻起，一切都只是理论。

entries.en: Necron's heart was beating so fast he could hear the palpitations. As he walked inside of the barrier, he was prudent in his actions, whether it be checking for magical traps or guards stationed on the inside.
entries.zh: 耐克伦的心跳快得能听见。走进屏障后，他的一举一动都十分谨慎，无论是检查魔法陷阱，还是留意驻守在内部的守卫。

entries.en: But once again, there was nothing. Maybe he was being too careful, whatever the case, he was certainly getting closer. A few hundred steps into the barrier, he felt it... An intense magic power that resonated with him.
entries.zh: 可又一次，什么都没有。也许他太过小心了，不管怎样，他确实越来越近了。深入屏障几百步后，他感觉到了……一股与他产生共鸣的强大魔力。

entries.en: This foul energy seemed to originate from ahead, and as he approached it, he noticed that the energy was corrupting everything around it, the ground itself had even turned to varying shades of gray.
entries.zh: 这股污秽的能量似乎来自前方，他越靠近，越发现这股能量正在侵蚀周围的一切，连地面都变成了深浅不一的灰色。

entries.en: The grass and earth around him seemed to have lacked color for a long time. After what felt like an eternity, he finally saw it. A large and robust magic cage, standing on the very corner of the island.
entries.zh: 他周围的草地和泥土似乎已经褪色很久了。仿佛过了一个世纪，他终于看到了它。一座巨大而坚固的魔法牢笼，矗立在岛屿的最边角。

entries.en: The cage was made of pillars in a circle, channeling a maelstrom of energy inside, like a blue tornado. Necron could barely see through the dense waves of magic, but what he could see was enough to push his sanity to its extreme limits.
entries.zh: 牢笼由一圈柱子组成，将一股能量漩涡导入其中，就像一道蓝色的龙卷风。透过密集的魔法波动，耐克伦几乎什么都看不清，但他所看到的已足以把他的理智逼到极限。

entries.en: An imposing creature at least twice his size, with giant ribs as thick as a grown man's arm, and three grotesque, dark shriveled heads, all distinct, yet expressionless. Only the middle one seemed to notice his presence.
entries.zh: 那是一个威严的生物，至少有他两倍高，巨大的肋骨像成年男子的手臂一样粗，还有三颗怪诞、干瘪的黑色头颅，各不相同，却都面无表情。只有中间那颗似乎注意到了他的存在。

entries.en: Necron thought himself to be mentally prepared, but his hands still shook from fear and hesitation. As he walked towards the cage, he heard it. A deep, raspy voice spoke from within the swirl of energy: "You are using my spell."
entries.zh: 耐克伦以为自己已经做好了心理准备，可他的双手仍因恐惧和犹豫而颤抖。他朝牢笼走去时，听到了那个声音。一个低沉、沙哑的声音从能量漩涡中传来：“你在用我的法术。”

entries.en: Necron stopped, he thought the Wither King would be able to speak, but it still came as a surprise. "Who are you, and why are you here?" the voice asked. "Why am I here?" Necron mumbled, becoming agitated.
entries.zh: 耐克伦停下了脚步，他原以为凋灵之王会说话，但这仍让他吃了一惊。“你是谁，为什么来这里？”那个声音问道。“我为什么来这里？”耐克伦喃喃自语，变得焦躁起来。

entries.en: He wanted to ask many questions, but when he gathered the courage to face his enemy, he couldn't rid himself of anxiety. "My name is Necron," his voice was unsteady, still shaken with fear.
entries.zh: 他有很多问题想问，可当他鼓起勇气面对敌人时，却怎么也摆脱不了焦虑。“我叫耐克伦，”他的声音不稳，仍因恐惧而发颤。

entries.en: "You killed my parents 17 years ago... My father was a war hero, and my mother protected me with her life!" Necron panted heavily, having cemented his name and burden to the Wither King. A brief silence ensued.
entries.zh: “17 年前你杀了我的父母……我父亲是战斗英雄，我母亲用生命保护了我！”耐克伦喘着粗气，向凋灵之王说出了自己的名字和背负的重担。一阵短暂的沉默。

entries.en: Necron tried to guess what this monster would say back to him, but he couldn't come up with anything. "Is that why you are here, Necron?" The Wither King answered. "No..." Necron refuted.
entries.zh: 耐克伦试着猜测这个怪物会怎么回答他，却什么也想不出来。“你就是为了这个来的吗，耐克伦？”凋灵之王答道。“不……”耐克伦否认道。

entries.en: "You said I was using your spell, what do you mean?" asked Necron.
entries.zh: “你说我在用你的法术，这是什么意思？”耐克伦问。

entries.en: "Fel magic, or a variant. I created that spell, and wrote the scroll myself."
entries.zh: “邪能魔法，或者说它的一种变体。那个法术是我创造的，卷轴也是我亲手写的。”

entries.en: "So the rumors are true, you were a human before, called Kaeman?"
entries.zh: “那么传言是真的，你以前是人类，名叫凯曼？”
“没错。”

entries.en: "Fel magic... What is it, and why do I have an affinity for it? Have you done anything to me?"
entries.zh: “邪能魔法……那是什么？为什么我会与它有亲和？你对我做过什么吗？”

entries.en: "I haven't. Well, at least not intentionally. I've never met anyone with an affinity for Fel magic, it is quite interesting."
entries.zh: “我没有。好吧，至少不是故意的。我从没见过有谁对邪能魔法有亲和，这很有意思。”

entries.en: The Wither King continued: "While I didn't invent that kind of magic, I was the first human to study it, directly from the Dragon's heart. But the Academy was against any kind of progress for the dark arts, they have their own agenda."
entries.zh: 凋灵之王继续说道：“这种魔法虽不是我发明的，但我是第一个研究它的人类，直接从巨龙的心脏中研究。可学院反对黑暗技艺的任何进步，他们有自己的盘算。”

entries.en: Necron couldn't help but think that this monster in front of him was a lot more human than he thought. Of course, it could just be a facade, but he enjoyed that they had the same opinions regarding the Academy.
entries.zh: 耐克伦不禁觉得，眼前这个怪物比他想象的更像人类。当然，这也可能只是伪装，但他很高兴他们对学院的看法一致。

entries.en: The difference between him and the Wither King was that of night and day, yet, the longer they talked, the more he found a resemblance. Surprisingly, he quickly grew some sort of respect for the creature.
entries.zh: 他和凋灵之王有着天壤之别，然而谈得越久，他越发现彼此之间的相似之处。出乎意料的是，他很快就对这个生物产生了某种敬意。

entries.en: The conversation went on for hours. Kaeman was willing to teach Necron the basics of dark magic, but if he wanted to learn any more than that, it would come at a price...
entries.zh: 谈话持续了好几个小时。凯曼愿意教耐克伦黑暗魔法的基础，但如果他想学更多，就得付出代价……

entries.en: He couldn't fully trust the Wither King for now, but his sense of revenge had already totally dissipated, replaced by the excitement of having finally found a mighty master, someone who could understand him.
entries.zh: 他现在还不能完全信任凋灵之王，但他的复仇之心已经完全消散，取而代之的是终于找到一位强大导师的兴奋，一个能理解他的人。

entries.en: Necron knew that allying himself to the Wither King was a cruel joke at best, but at least he would be able to use dark magic, which he had an unnatural affinity towards. With the matter settled, he took his leave.
entries.zh: 耐克伦知道，与凋灵之王结盟充其量是个残酷的笑话，但至少他能使用黑暗魔法，而他对这种魔法有着非同寻常的亲和。事情谈妥后，他便告辞离开了。

entries.en: For many weeks in a row, Necron sacrificed sleep to come back, continuing his conversations with Kaeman, oftentimes going deep into the night. He had learned so much already but was only consumed by his desire to know more.
entries.zh: 接连好几周，耐克伦牺牲睡眠回到那里，继续与凯曼交谈，常常一直谈到深夜。他已经学到了很多，却只被想知道更多的欲望所吞噬。

entries.en: So when the time came for Necron to help Kaeman in return for more teachings, he immediately agreed to the request. Kaeman wanted to escape, and to that end, he came up with a spell that could destabilize the magic barrier.
entries.zh: 所以，当耐克伦需要帮助凯曼来换取更多教导时，他立刻答应了这个请求。凯曼想要逃出去，为此他想出了一个能扰乱魔法屏障的法术。

entries.en: Although the spell would only last for a few seconds, it was by far the most complex and intense spell Necron ever had to conjure. He positioned himself on the south-east section of the cage and began to work it out.
entries.zh: 虽然这个法术只能维持几秒钟，但它是耐克伦施放过的最复杂、最强烈的法术，没有之一。他站在牢笼的东南侧，开始施法。

entries.en: At first, there was a small disturbance in the cage, then a ripple in the barrier's energy waves. Necron was perturbed, surely the magicians sensed it. But it didn't matter, the spell was almost complete, and then...
entries.zh: 起初，牢笼里出现了一点小小的扰动，接着屏障的能量波泛起一阵涟漪。耐克伦心神不宁，法师们肯定察觉到了。但这已经无关紧要，法术就快完成了，然后……

entries.en: Tremendous energy poured from the Wither King. The disturbance in the cage became a turmoil, and quickly a hole appeared, growing visibly, the barrier in the skies distorting and twisting itself around it.
entries.zh: 巨大的能量从凋灵之王身上倾泻而出。牢笼中的扰动变成了一场动荡，很快出现了一个洞，并肉眼可见地扩大，空中的屏障围绕着它扭曲、翻卷。

entries.en: After a flash of light, the barrier was no more. "Quickly!" Kaeman exclaimed. He left the cage and fired a bolt of dark energy at the ground, not only breaking pillars from the cage but also part of the island itself.
entries.zh: 一道闪光过后，屏障消失了。“快！”凯曼喊道。他离开牢笼，朝地面射出一道黑暗能量，不仅击碎了牢笼的柱子，还炸掉了岛屿的一部分。

entries.en: Kaeman grabbed Necron then jumped into the void, but about a hundred meters deep the Wither stopped their fall and took the direction of a small opening on the cliff. As soon as they entered, he sealed the passage.
entries.zh: 凯曼抓住耐克伦，纵身跳入虚空，但下坠约一百米后，凋灵止住了他们的坠落，朝悬崖上的一个小洞口飞去。他们一进去，他就封住了通道。

entries.en: "Just what is... What is this place?" Necron exclaimed. The Wither King's acute sense of death had identified that his cage was right above a place filled with corpses. "The Catacombs." Kaeman replied.
entries.zh: “这……这到底是什么地方？”耐克伦惊呼。凋灵之王对死亡的敏锐感知早已察觉到，他的牢笼正好位于一个满是尸体的地方的上方。“地下墓穴。”凯曼答道。

entries.en: He had planned his escape to look like an accident, a bi-product of his planning. While hidden in the Catacombs he would have time to heal and prepare his return, while he taught his new apprentice from the shadows.
entries.zh: 他把这次逃脱安排得像一场意外，是他计划的副产品。藏身地下墓穴期间，他有时间疗伤、准备卷土重来，同时在暗中教导他的新学徒。
追随者 2

entries.en: Shortly after depositing the letter, Lathrop took the road that led to the Inn near the bottom of the Mountain. It was getting very dark and those roads were not safe at night, many people went missing in the last couple of years.
entries.zh: 送完信后不久，拉斯罗普沿着通往山脚旅馆的路走去。天已经很黑了，这些路在夜里并不安全，过去几年里有很多人失踪。

entries.en: Ever since the mysterious explosion of the Wither King's cage and its disappearance, strange events started to unfold on the island. While everyone is certain the creature fell in the void, many fear that the events are related.
entries.zh: 自从凋灵之王的牢笼发生神秘爆炸、凋灵之王随之消失后，岛上就开始出现怪事。虽然所有人都确信那个怪物掉进了虚空，但很多人担心这些事件之间有所关联。

entries.en: As Lathrop approached the Inn, a silhouette entered before him, and he got an impression of deja vu. Inside the building the atmosphere was jovial, music was playing and a few people were apparently having some sort of contest.
entries.zh: 拉斯罗普走近旅馆时，一个身影在他前面走了进去，他产生了一种似曾相识的感觉。旅馆里的气氛很欢快，音乐正在演奏，几个人似乎在进行某种比赛。

entries.en: Lathrop looked for a table on the side where it would be quiet and waited for the waitress. When he looked around, he noticed that in the opposite corner from him, the person he saw before was sitting alone as well.
entries.zh: 拉斯罗普在角落里找了张安静的桌子，等着女招待过来。他环顾四周，发现在他对面的角落里，他之前看到的那个人也独自坐着。

entries.en: They were wearing black clothes and had dark hair. The man had a long cape as well, and there was an odd square-like shape underneath it, obviously something they wanted to keep hidden from the common eye.
entries.zh: 那人穿着一身黑衣，留着黑发。他还披着一件长斗篷，斗篷下面有一个奇怪的方形轮廓，显然是不想让旁人看见的东西。

entries.en: It was then that his feeling of deja vu became much more clear, he had seen this exact scene before in a vision! Although he could not remember much of it, he knew he was supposed to do something.
entries.zh: 就在这时，他那种似曾相识的感觉变得清晰起来，他在一个幻象中见过这一模一样的场景！虽然记不太清细节，但他知道自己应该做些什么。

entries.en: The waitress came and Lathrop ordered a meal, but he couldn't stop himself from watching the strange man. Eventually, after another half hour, the man left his table and took the stairs for a room, where he would spend the night.
entries.zh: 女招待过来了，拉斯罗普点了一份餐，但他忍不住一直盯着那个奇怪的男人。又过了半个小时，那人终于离开桌子，走上楼梯去房间过夜。

entries.en: Almost as soon as that happened, a man with dark skin joined his table without asking permission. They looked tipsy, Lathrop thought that staying with them would mean trouble, so he got up to leave.
entries.zh: 几乎就在同时，一个深色皮肤的男人没经允许就坐到了他的桌旁。那人看起来有些醉意，拉斯罗普觉得和他待在一起准没好事，于是起身要走。

entries.en: "Hey!" The man advanced towards Lathrop. "You look like a nice fellow. It's just that I saw how you looked at the man who just left, do you know them? Never seen them round here before, and I'm good with faces!"
entries.zh: “嘿！”那人朝拉斯罗普走过来，“你看上去是个好人。只是我看到你一直盯着刚才离开的那个人，你认识他吗？我以前从没在这附近见过他，我可是很会认人的！”

entries.en: As the man was speaking, he stumbled backward, almost losing his balance. "Whoops... Maybe I had too much to drink? Heh." The man's words echoed in Lathrop's head. 'I've seen this before, in my dreams!'
entries.zh: 那人说着说着，往后踉跄了一下，差点没站稳。“哎呀……我是不是喝多了？嘿嘿。”那人的话在拉斯罗普的脑海中回响。‘我见过这一幕，在我的梦里！’

entries.en: Suddenly, and entirely out of his control, words flew from his mouth. "Yeah, I know him, just a merchant from far away who I had some business with before." Lathrop felt a shiver down his spine. 'Why did I say that?' he thought.
entries.zh: 突然，完全不受他控制，话就从他嘴里冒了出来。“是啊，我认识他，他只是个远道而来的商人，我以前跟他做过生意。”拉斯罗普感到脊背一阵发凉。‘我为什么要这么说？’他想。

entries.en: The man looked at him, "Mmm, glad he's not some kind of trouble or something! These days you never know, we live in a strange time. Sorry for the bother, I'll leave you alone." and he took his cup, then went back to sit at his table.
entries.zh: 那人看着他：“嗯，还好他不是什么麻烦人物！这年头谁也说不准，我们活在一个奇怪的时代。抱歉打扰你了，我不烦你了。”说完他拿起杯子，回到自己的桌旁坐下。

entries.en: Lathrop left a few coins on the counter and asked the hostess for a room. A few minutes later, he was in a nice bed ready to sleep for the night, but he just couldn't shake this feeling, that something was about to happen.
entries.zh: 拉斯罗普在柜台上放下几枚硬币，向老板娘要了一个房间。几分钟后，他已经躺在舒适的床上准备睡觉，可他就是摆脱不了一种感觉，觉得有什么事就要发生了。
杀手

entries.en: At about 15 years of age, Livid was already counted among the most gifted members in the Guild of Thieves. A street boy who went from stealing fruits from peddler's carts to a full-blown membership in the Guild.
entries.zh: 大约 15 岁时，利维德就已跻身盗贼公会最有天赋的成员之列。一个流浪街头的男孩，从偷小贩推车上的水果开始，一路成了公会的正式成员。

entries.en: When he turned 17, the Guild's leader gave him his first assassination contract. A merchant paid a substantial amount for his competition to disappear, permanently. And Livid, despite his young age, had been chosen for the task.
entries.zh: 他 17 岁那年，公会首领给了他第一份暗杀合约。一个商人花重金要让自己的竞争对手永远消失。而利维德尽管年纪轻轻，却被选中执行这项任务。

entries.en: Livid was certainly an exceptional thief, but that night he found out he was an even better assassin, and this newfound vocation grew in him, quickly becoming what he would call art. And every kill was his new masterpiece...
entries.zh: 利维德无疑是个出色的盗贼，但那天晚上他发现，自己是个更出色的刺客。这份新发现的天职在他心中不断滋长，很快成了他所说的艺术。而每一次杀戮，都是他的新杰作……

entries.en: He would often talk about his contracts in gruesome detail with the other members of the guild, who hated it, so much so that they tried to 'remove' him from the guild. Unexpectedly, they were the ones 'removed.'
entries.zh: 他经常向公会里的其他成员绘声绘色地讲述他的合约细节，大家都很反感，甚至想把他从公会里“清除”出去。出乎意料的是，被“清除”的反而是他们。

entries.en: Over the years he refined his technique, but he would eliminate his targets so easily that he could barely take away any pride in those assassinations. He was now looking for high-profile prey, some he would struggle with.
entries.zh: 多年来，他不断精进自己的技艺，可他解决目标太过轻松，几乎无法从这些暗杀中获得任何成就感。现在他在寻找重量级的猎物，那种能让他费一番功夫的目标。

entries.en: That night, a mantle of heavy fog had rolled in down the mountainside, enshrouding the entire forest as well as the Inn nearby. Normal sounds were muffled, and everything seemed more subdued than usual.
entries.zh: 那天晚上，一层浓雾从山坡上弥漫下来，笼罩了整片森林和附近的旅馆。平常的声音都变得沉闷，一切似乎都比往常更加压抑。

entries.en: For Livid, the night's conditions were ideal. Tonight he would hunt, and the Inn was the perfect place to start. It was rather crowded, and at first glance, he couldn't scout any prime victim, so he sat at a table and ordered a drink.
entries.zh: 对利维德来说，那晚的条件再理想不过。今晚他要狩猎，而旅馆正是开始的绝佳地点。旅馆里人很多，乍一看他没发现什么上好的猎物，于是找了张桌子坐下，点了一杯酒。

entries.en: An hour later, a mysterious man wearing a large black cape entered the Inn and went straight to a corner table, not making eye contact with anyone. Livid's attention turned towards what was under his cape, which looked like a small chest.
entries.zh: 一个小时后，一个披着宽大黑斗篷的神秘男人走进旅馆，径直走向角落的一张桌子，没有和任何人对视。利维德的注意力转向了他斗篷下面的东西，看起来像一个小箱子。

entries.en: Almost immediately after, another man came in and sat down at a table on the opposite side, then proceeded to study the individual with the black cape for almost an hour, which intrigued Livid even more.
entries.zh: 几乎紧接着，另一个男人走了进来，在对面的一张桌子旁坐下，然后盯着那个披黑斗篷的人看了将近一个小时，这让利维德更感兴趣了。

entries.en: He had to find out who those people were. From what he could tell, the second man was not a threat, but definitely had valuable information regarding his potential target. Suddenly, the man with the cape left his table and went upstairs.
entries.zh: 他必须弄清楚这两个人是谁。据他判断，第二个男人构不成威胁，但肯定掌握着关于他潜在目标的宝贵信息。突然，披斗篷的男人离开桌子上了楼。

entries.en: Livid walked towards the second man, pretending to have had a few drinks, and questioned him about the caped fellow, which turned out to be a merchant from far away. He couldn't ask for a better target! It was settled, tonight, he would kill.
entries.zh: 利维德朝第二个男人走去，装作喝了几杯的样子，向他打听那个披斗篷的家伙，结果对方是个远道而来的商人。再没有比这更好的目标了！就这么定了，今晚，他要杀人。

entries.en: The merchant's room was towards the left side of the Inn. The faint glow from a distant streetlamp illuminated the open window. With economical movements, Livid climbed the few meters separating him from the window.
entries.zh: 商人的房间在旅馆的左侧。远处一盏路灯的微光照亮了敞开的窗户。利维德动作干净利落，爬过了他与窗户之间那几米的距离。

entries.en: A quick pull and he was sitting on the edge of the window. As he previously analyzed, the room was quiet and the merchant was asleep. Livid peered around, his other senses aiding his search, but no sign of the chest.
entries.zh: 轻轻一拉，他就坐到了窗沿上。正如他之前判断的那样，房间里很安静，商人已经睡着了。利维德四下张望，调动其他感官帮忙搜寻，但没有发现箱子的踪影。

entries.en: Unable to locate a safe place to walk without making any sound, Livid pulled out his dagger, he would have to kill the merchant before entering the room. The blade between his fingers, he readied his arm in striking position.
entries.zh: 找不到能悄无声息落脚的地方，利维德抽出了匕首，他必须在进房间之前杀死商人。他把刀刃夹在指间，抬起手臂摆好出手的姿势。

entries.en: His concentration was halted by a sound coming from the right corner of the room that he had already inspected. One thing he knew; sound does not come from thin air - except when magic is at play.
entries.zh: 就在这时，房间右侧角落传来一个声音，打断了他的专注，而那个角落他已经检查过了。有一点他很清楚：声音不会凭空出现——除非有魔法在作祟。

entries.en: Livid froze in place, holding his breath. The body in the bed was gone, he had been fooled! Before he could do anything, a sharp blade was running through his body. He could feel the steel cutting his heart in half.
entries.zh: 利维德僵在原地，屏住了呼吸。床上的人不见了，他被骗了！还没等他做出任何反应，一把锋利的剑刃就刺穿了他的身体。他能感觉到钢刃把他的心脏一劈为二。

entries.en: 'So this is it.' He thought, and he looked at the man holding the sword: young, but his face deeply marked, as if his skin was mixed with some sort of gray dust. This was no merchant, he was facing a mage, and a powerful one.
entries.zh: ‘原来就是这样。’他想着，看向持剑的人：很年轻，但脸上布满深深的痕迹，皮肤仿佛混进了某种灰色的尘土。这不是什么商人，他面对的是一名法师，而且是一名强大的法师。

entries.en: The blade was pulled out, it had inscriptions and motives on the edge. No blood flowed, and Livid couldn't feel his body anymore. "H-how am I still alive?" He wailed. "What did you do to me?!" Then, he fell on the ground, unconscious.
entries.zh: 剑被拔了出来，剑刃上刻着铭文和图案。没有血流出来，利维德已经感觉不到自己的身体了。“我……我怎么还活着？”他哀号着，“你对我做了什么？！”然后，他倒在地上，失去了知觉。

entries.en: The misty veil of fog slowly lifted, yet the night still obscured the path ahead. Lathrop followed the mysterious stranger from a distance, his silhouette barely visible in the darkness. The man now seemed to be carrying another, the one from the inn.
entries.zh: 雾气慢慢散去，但夜色依旧遮蔽着前方的道路。拉斯罗普远远地跟着那个神秘的陌生人，他的身影在黑暗中几乎看不见。那人现在似乎扛着另一个人，正是旅馆里的那个。

entries.en: The sensation of deja vu was growing stronger with each step. Though he could not recall ever having witnessed it before in his visions. The man ventured on towards the coal cavern nestled deep within the shadowy woods.
entries.zh: 似曾相识的感觉随着每一步越来越强烈。可他想不起自己曾在幻象中见过这一幕。那人朝着藏在幽暗森林深处的煤矿洞穴走去。

entries.en: Stepping cautiously into the cave, Lathrop removed his boots, wary of the sound resonating on the walls. The stranger and his burden were now out of sight, yet the sound of their progress still echoed through the cavern's corridors.
entries.zh: 拉斯罗普小心翼翼地走进洞穴，脱下靴子，以防脚步声在洞壁间回荡。陌生人和他扛着的人已经看不见了，但他们前进的声音仍在洞穴的通道中回响。

entries.en: Lathrop descended one of the corridors, the footsteps before him his only guide. Suspicion grew as to their destination - the coal cave was an entrance to the ancient Catacombs, final resting place of the Cataclysm's casualties.
entries.zh: 拉斯罗普走下其中一条通道，前方的脚步声是他唯一的向导。他越来越怀疑他们的目的地——这个煤矿洞穴是古老地下墓穴的入口，大灾变遇难者的最终安息之所。

entries.en: Echoes faded, Lathrop waited in silence, ears pricked for any sign of his quarry's passage. After a moment deemed safe, he resumed his pursuit. At last, he arrived in a large chamber, the catacomb's gateway. The stranger was nowhere in sight.
entries.zh: 回声渐渐消失，拉斯罗普静静等待，竖起耳朵留意猎物经过的任何动静。等到觉得安全了，他又继续追踪。最后，他来到一个巨大的墓室，那是地下墓穴的大门。陌生人不见了踪影。

entries.en: Lathrop was about to inspect the grand wooden door in front of him, when a voice shattered the silence from behind him. "Why are you trailing me?" It asked, causing a chill to run down his spine.
entries.zh: 拉斯罗普正要查看面前那扇宏伟的木门，身后突然传来一个声音，打破了寂静。“你为什么跟着我？”那个声音问道，让他脊背一阵发凉。

entries.en: His fear receded as he turned to face the man from the inn, and the large body next to him. The sensation of deja vu reached its peak and the same feeling he had at the inn overtook him. "I must," he muttered, "I have seen you in visions."
entries.zh: 他转过身，面对旅馆里的那个男人和他身旁那具高大的身躯，恐惧渐渐退去。似曾相识的感觉达到了顶点，他在旅馆里的那种感觉再次涌上心头。“我必须这么做，”他喃喃道，“我在幻象中见过你。”

entries.en: "You speak of visions," Necron said, visibly intrigued. "What is it that you have seen in these visions?"
entries.zh: “你说起幻象，”耐克伦说，显然起了兴趣，“你在这些幻象里看到了什么？”

entries.en: "I have seen that by following you to your master, I will reach the full extent of my abilities," Lathrop replied.
entries.zh: “我看到，只要跟着你去见你的主人，我就能发挥出自己全部的能力。”拉斯罗普回答。

entries.en: Necron observed Lathrop in silence for a moment, then picked up Livid's unconscious body and slung it over his shoulder. He walked towards the large wooden door, which opened on its own. "Come," he said as he stepped into the Catacombs.
entries.zh: 耐克伦沉默地打量了拉斯罗普片刻，然后扛起利维德昏迷的身体，甩到肩上。他朝那扇巨大的木门走去，门自己打开了。“来吧，”他说着，走进了地下墓穴。
